issue.title: [17.0][FIX] product_brand: fix error on clicking brand in product kanban view
issue.body:
This fixes the following error:

```
EvalError: Can not evaluate python expression: ([('product_ids', 'in', id)])
    Error: Name 'id' is not defined
    EvalError: Can not evaluate python expression: ([('product_ids', 'in', id)])
    Error: Name 'id' is not defined
        at evaluateExpr (http://oca-brand-17-0-1589852de24e.runboat.odoo-community.org/web/assets/83b0f05/web.assets_web.min.js:3043:54)
        at _preprocessAction (http://oca-brand-17-0-1589852de24e.runboat.odoo-community.org/web/assets/83b0f05/web.assets_web.min.js:10184:150)
        at doAction (http://oca-brand-17-0-1589852de24e.runboat.odoo-community.org/web/assets/83b0f05/web.assets_web.min.js:10266:170)
        at async Object.doActionButton (http://oca-brand-17-0-1589852de24e.runboat.odoo-community.org/web/assets/83b0f05/web.assets_web.min.js:10274:196)
        at async execute (http://oca-brand-17-0-1589852de24e.runboat.odoo-community.org/web/assets/83b0f05/web.assets_web.min.js:9898:293)
        at async executeButtonCallback (http://oca-brand-17-0-1589852de24e.runboat.odoo-community.org/web/assets/83b0f05/web.assets_web.min.js:9891:34)
```


Steps to reproduce in runbot:

 - go to Invoicing > Products, open one product form and add a brand to the product
 - open the kanban view of products, the brand is shown in the kanban tile of that product
 - click on the brand link: the error is displayed

Prettier doesn't treat U+30A0 & U+30FB as Japanese. U+30FB is commonly used in Japanese to represent the delimitation of first and last names of non-Japanese people or “and”. The following “C言語・C++・Go・Rust” means “C language & C++ & Go & Rust” in Japanese.

issue.title: [Improvement suggestion] Lock on map zoom level
issue.body:
I currently use this feature from [explore.osmaps.com](https://explore.osmaps.com) where I can lock the map on a specific zoom level on the topographic map type:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/72685c9a-5dc8-4926-bd2b-59cf66d38fc6)

I use this:
- for planning my routes on a more detailed level, while still being able to zoom out and get the detailed overview for a big area
- but also the other way around, to lock the zoom on a less detailed level, while zooming in. This situation is especially useful for long-distance hikes, where I want to write down a route description based on the 1:50k maps

As the long-distance hikes that I plan, are using lesser used (unofficial) paths, I believe the following features would be useful related to the lock map on zoom level:
- Ability to lock a map type on a specific zoom level (same as what OSmaps supports)
- Ability to lock all map types on the same specific zoom level; which is useful when switching map types a lot (which I do :sweat_smile: )
- Ability to lock each map type to a specific zoom level (which can be different per map)
- And inherent to above options, locked zoom levels should be remembered between map switches

(I hope/assume, most maps will have similar zoom levels :crossed_fingers: )

What do you think? Would this fit your vision of the project?

Fix handling of orphaned 2PC files in the future at recovery

Before 728bd991c3c4, that has improved the support for 2PC files during
recovery, the initial logic scanning files in pg_twophase was done so as
files in the future of the transaction ID horizon were checked first,
followed by a check if a transaction ID is aborted or committed which
could involve a pg_xact lookup.  After this commit, these checks have
been done in reverse order.

Files detected as in the future do not have a state that can be checked
in pg_xact, hence this caused recovery to fail abruptly should an
orphaned 2PC file in the future of the transaction ID horizon exist in
pg_twophase at the beginning of recovery.

A test is added to check for this scenario, using an empty 2PC with a
transaction ID large enough to be in the future when running the test.
This test is added in 16 and older versions for now.  17 and newer
versions are impacted by a second bug caused by the addition of the
epoch in the 2PC file names.  An equivalent test will be added in these
branches in a follow-up commit, once the second set of issues reported
are fixed.

Fix failures with incorrect epoch handling for 2PC files at recovery

At the beginning of recovery, an orphaned two-phase file in an epoch
different than the one defined in the checkpoint record could not be
removed based on the assumptions that AdjustToFullTransactionId() relies
on, assuming that all files would be either from the current epoch or
from the previous epoch.

If the checkpoint epoch was 0 while the 2PC file was orphaned and in the
future, AdjustToFullTransactionId() would underflow the epoch used to
build the 2PC file path.  In non-assert builds, this would create a
WARNING message referring to a 2PC file with an epoch of "FFFFFFFF" (or
UINT32_MAX), as an effect of the underflow calculation, leaving the
orphaned file around.

Some tests are added with dummy 2PC files in the past and the future,
checking that these are properly removed.

Issue introduced by 5a1dfde8334b, that has switched two-phase state
files to use FullTransactionIds.

Fix memory leak in pgoutput with relation attribute map

pgoutput caches the attribute map of a relation, that is free()'d only
when validating a RelationSyncEntry.  However, this code path is not
taken when calling any of the SQL functions able to do some logical
decoding, like pg_logical_slot_{get,peek}_changes(), leaking some memory

PGOutputData's cachectx, free()'d at the end of the execution of these
SQL functions when logical decoding ends.  This is available down to 15.

checked on a per-row basis when sending field representations in text

# Code Review: ZLMediaKit SrtPusher.h header file

## Summary

This review assesses the `SrtPusher.h` header file, a new addition to the ZLMediaKit project. The review focuses on code structure, design choices, and adherence to best practices.

## Detailed Feedback

### Code Overview

The header file defines `SrtPusher`, a class inheriting from `PusherBase` and `SrtCaller`, implementing SRT-based media streaming.  It handles publishing streams via SRT, including handshake management and error handling.

### Strengths

- **Clear Inheritance:** The use of inheritance from `PusherBase` and `SrtCaller` is a good design choice, promoting code reuse and organization.
- **Use of Smart Pointers:**  The use of `std::shared_ptr` for `SrtPusher` and `std::weak_ptr` for `_push_src` demonstrates good memory management practices, preventing memory leaks.
- **Well-Defined Interface:** The public interface clearly exposes the necessary methods for publishing and tearing down streams.
- **Includes Necessary Headers:** The header file includes all necessary headers for compilation.


### Areas for Improvement

#### 1.  Missing Documentation

- **Issue:** The header file lacks detailed documentation explaining the purpose and usage of each member function and class member.  This makes understanding the code's functionality difficult.
- **Suggestion:** Add comprehensive Doxygen-style comments to document the class, its members, and their functionalities.  Explain the parameters, return values, and any potential exceptions.
- **Example:**
  ```c++
  /**
   * @brief Constructs a new SrtPusher object.
   * 
   * @param poller The event poller to use for network operations.
   * @param src The media source to push.
   */
  SrtPusher(const toolkit::EventPoller::Ptr &poller, const TSMediaSource::Ptr &src);
  ```

#### 2.  Unclear `doPublish()` Function

- **Issue:** The `doPublish()` function is declared but not defined in the header file.  Its implementation is likely in a `.cpp` file, but its purpose and functionality are unclear without seeing the implementation.
- **Suggestion:**  Briefly describe the purpose of `doPublish()` in a comment within the header file.  This will improve readability and understanding.

#### 3.  Potential for Race Conditions

- **Issue:** Without seeing the implementation, there's a potential for race conditions if multiple threads access or modify the `_push_src` and `_ts_reader` members concurrently.
- **Suggestion:**  Consider using appropriate synchronization mechanisms (e.g., mutexes, atomic variables) to protect shared resources from concurrent access.  This is crucial for thread safety.

#### 4.  Error Handling

- **Issue:** While the code handles exceptions via `onResult`, the specific error handling strategy is not clear.  What happens when an error occurs during publishing?  How are errors reported to the user or application?
- **Suggestion:**  Implement robust error handling, including logging of errors and appropriate responses to different error scenarios.  Consider using a more sophisticated error reporting mechanism than just `toolkit::SockException`.

#### 5.  Missing Configuration Options

- **Issue:** The class currently lacks configurable parameters (e.g., SRT latency, timeout, buffer size).  This limits flexibility and customization.
- **Suggestion:**  Add configurable parameters to allow users to fine-tune the SRT connection based on their network conditions and application requirements.  These could be passed in the constructor or via setter methods.


## Conclusion

The `SrtPusher.h` header file provides a good foundation for SRT-based media streaming. However, improvements are needed in documentation, error handling, thread safety, and configurability to enhance robustness, maintainability, and usability.  Addressing the points raised above will significantly improve the code's quality and reliability.

pull_request.title: Dev
pull_request.body:
Solution for Day8.

In the first part a network of nodes is traversed from a start node to an end node with a given path. The steps to reach the final node are counted and this number gives the solution.

The second part complicates this significantly by requiring to start from six nodes using the same path at the same time where each of those node needs a different amount of steps to reach an end node. Thus, getting to a state where all nodes are end nodes requires many cycles of the same path and trillions of steps. This means any iterative/brute force attempt to solve the puzzle takes forever and a more straightforward way to solve the problem is to first calculate the amount of steps for each start node and then find the LCM (Least Common Multiple).

General Overview:

- "aoc8.py" is the entry point that prints the solutions for part one and two.
- "Network" class contains all the required methods to solve the puzzle (including technically correct but super inefficient iterative brute force methods)
- "Counter" is a new utility helper to pass a mutable counter
- "benchmark_helper" provides benchmark printouts for function runtime

Solution for Day8. (#15)

Solution for Day8.

In the first part a network of nodes is traversed from a start node to an end node with a given path. The steps to reach the final node are counted and this number gives the solution.

The second part complicates this significantly by requiring to start from six nodes using the same path at the same time where each of those node needs a different amount of steps to reach an end node. Thus, getting to a state where all nodes are end nodes requires many cycles of the same path and trillions of steps. This means any iterative/brute force attempt to solve the puzzle takes forever and a more straightforward way to solve the problem is to first calculate the amount of steps for each start node and then find the LCM (Least Common Multiple).

General Overview:

- "aoc8.py" is the entry point that prints the solutions for part one and two.
- "Network" class contains all the required methods to solve the puzzle (including technically correct but super inefficient iterative brute force methods)
- "Counter" is a new utility helper to pass a mutable counter
- "benchmark_helper" provides benchmark printouts for function runtime
